pages.title: About Spring
pages.description: Spring is a fintech infrastructure company transforming mortgage banking in Nigeria, in partnership with AG Mortgage Bank.

sections.heading: The infrastructure behind Africa’s mortgage revolution.
sections.subheading: Spring is a fintech infrastructure company transforming mortgage banking in Nigeria. In partnership with AG Mortgage Bank, we provide the backbone that lets businesses, fintechs, and real estate firms embed mortgage services seamlessly.

sections.heading: Born to break the barriers.
sections.body:
Nigeria faces a housing deficit of over 20 million units. Yet mortgage penetration is less than 1%. Direct-to-consumer banking models are too slow and too expensive. Building compliant, licensed financial products from the ground up is slow, capital-intensive, and operationally complex for most institutions in Africa.

Licensed institutions often have regulatory capacity but lack the technology, distribution reach, or customer experience layer to bring products to market at scale. Distribution partners have access to end users but no licensed capacity to originate financial products directly. End users are underserved by processes that are opaque, paper-based, and slow.

Spring was born to break these barriers.

pages.title: Privacy Policy — Spring
pages.description: How Spring collects, protects, and respects your data.

sections.heading: We take your privacy seriously.
sections.subheading: Spring collects only the data necessary to process mortgages, onboard businesses, and improve user experience.

sections.heading: Your Data, Your Control
sections.body:
You can request, export, or delete your information at any time. Spring collects only the data necessary to process mortgages, onboard businesses, and improve the user experience — nothing more.

Data we collect is limited to identity and eligibility information required by our licensed partners to originate financial products, business information required to onboard partners, and anonymised usage signals that help us improve the platform.

sections.heading: Security First
sections.body:
We use bank-grade encryption across every layer of the platform and comply with the Nigeria Data Protection Regulation (NDPR).

Every Spring wallet maps one-to-one to a real account held at a CBN-licensed financial institution. Customer funds are never held by Spring.

sections.heading: No Hidden Sharing
sections.body:
We never sell your data. Partners only access what is needed to serve you better.

Data is shared exclusively with the licensed financial institutions originating your products and the distribution partner through whom you accessed them — always under strict contractual and regulatory obligations.

sections.heading: Your Rights
sections.body:
Under the NDPR you have the right to access your personal data, request correction of inaccurate data, request deletion of your data, and withdraw consent at any time.

To exercise any of these rights, contact us at privacy@spring.ng. We respond to all verified requests within 30 days.

sections.heading: Questions about your data?
sections.body: Our team is ready to help with any privacy request.

pages.title: Terms & Conditions — Spring
pages.description: The terms governing use of the Spring platform.

sections.heading: Clear terms. Binding trust.
sections.subheading: By using Spring’s platform, you agree to the following terms.

sections.heading: 1. Licensing & Compliance
sections.body:
Mortgage processing on Spring is powered by AG Mortgage Bank for compliance and licensing, alongside Charis MFB and Fortress Capital — all Central Bank of Nigeria-licensed institutions.

Every account and every transaction on Spring’s infrastructure is legally held and owned by a licensed financial institution, which retains full legal ownership of the customer relationship and funds.

sections.heading: 2. Nature of the Service
sections.body:
Spring provides infrastructure, not financial advice. Spring is not a bank, lender, or deposit-taking institution. Spring’s role is strictly limited to technology, orchestration, and distribution — Spring does not underwrite, lend, or hold customer funds.

Eligibility decisions, product terms, and regulatory obligations rest with the originating licensed institution.

sections.heading: 3. Fees & Commissions
sections.body:
Fees, commissions, and integrations are transparent and binding. Integration fees are agreed before onboarding, and Spring earns a fair take-rate on transactions orchestrated through the infrastructure.

No hidden charges will ever be introduced. Any change to fees is communicated in advance and in writing.

sections.heading: 4. Partner Obligations
sections.body:
All partners must comply with Nigerian mortgage and data protection laws, including the Nigeria Data Protection Regulation (NDPR).

Partners are responsible for the accuracy of information they submit, for representing products fairly to their audiences, and for maintaining the confidentiality of their integration credentials.

sections.heading: 5. Acceptable Use
sections.body:
You agree not to misuse the platform, attempt to reverse engineer the infrastructure, misrepresent Spring’s regulatory status, or use the platform for any unlawful purpose.

Spring may suspend access for any breach of these terms, with notice and an opportunity to remedy where appropriate.

posts.title: Why Nigeria Needs Mortgage Infrastructure, Not More Banks
posts.excerpt: Nigeria’s housing deficit exceeds 20 million units while mortgage penetration sits below 1%. The bottleneck isn’t demand — it’s the rails.
posts.content:
Nigeria faces a housing deficit of over 20 million units. Yet mortgage penetration is less than 1%. The instinctive policy response is to call for more mortgage banks. But the direct-to-consumer banking model is precisely what has failed: it is too slow, too expensive, and too far from the customer.

What Nigeria needs is infrastructure — shared rails that let any licensed institution originate mortgages and any trusted business distribute them. That is the layer Spring is building.

When a real estate firm can offer mortgages under its own brand, when a cooperative can give members access to housing finance, when a bank can scale distribution without scaling overhead, the market compounds. Each new participant makes the network more valuable for everyone else.

The future of mortgages in Africa is not more banks. It is better rails.

posts.title: How Churches and Cooperatives Can Power Home Ownership
posts.excerpt: The most trusted institutions in Nigerian communities are not banks. They are churches, cooperatives, and social groups — and they can become mortgage hubs.
posts.content:
Trust is the scarcest resource in Nigerian finance. And the institutions that hold it — churches, cooperatives, and community organisations — have historically been locked out of formal financial distribution.

Spring changes that. With a community subdomain, a cooperative or church can create its own mortgage service hub: branded, mobile-first, and backed by the regulatory license of AG Mortgage Bank.

Members access mortgage products through an institution they already trust. The community organisation earns a fair commission. And housing becomes a community benefit, not a distant banking product.

This is what embedded finance looks like when it meets African social structure: housing as a community benefit, powered by infrastructure that does the heavy lifting.

posts.title: The Flutterwave Playbook: What Mortgages Can Learn
posts.excerpt: Payments scaled in Africa when infrastructure abstracted away complexity. Mortgages are next — and the playbook is already written.
posts.content:
Before Flutterwave, accepting payments across Africa meant negotiating with banks, processors, and regulators one by one. Infrastructure changed everything: integrate once, reach everywhere.

Mortgages are where payments were a decade ago. Every institution that wants to offer housing finance faces the same wall: licensing, origination systems, compliance, distribution. Each builds alone, slowly, at enormous cost.

Spring applies the same playbook to mortgages. One integration. Licensed rails. Distribution through every trusted channel — banks, fintechs, real estate firms, cooperatives, employers.

Our vision is explicit: to be the Flutterwave for Mortgage — the trusted infrastructure powering Africa’s mortgage revolution.

posts.title: Mortgage 2030: Data, AI, and Africa’s Housing Revolution
posts.excerpt: Real-time eligibility, data-driven underwriting signals, and mobile-first journeys will define the next decade of African housing finance.
posts.content:
The mortgage process in much of Africa remains opaque, paper-based, and slow. First-time buyers, salaried professionals, and diaspora Nigerians are underserved by journeys that were never designed for them.

The next decade will be defined by three shifts. First, data: real-time insights into customer needs will let institutions design products that actually fit. Second, intelligence: eligibility checks and risk signals that today take weeks will happen in seconds. Third, experience: mobile-first, transparent, guided journeys will replace branch visits and paper files.

Spring is building for that decade today — real-time status tracking, data-driven analytics for partners, and a white-labelled PWA that meets users where they already are.

Mortgage 2030 is not a prediction. It is a roadmap.

faqs.question: Can individuals apply directly through Spring?
faqs.answer: No. You’ll access Spring-powered mortgages through our partner merchants, banks, and institutions — where you already shop, bank, or worship.

faqs.question: How safe is my data?
faqs.answer: We use bank-grade security and comply with the Nigeria Data Protection Regulation (NDPR). We never sell your data, and partners only access what’s needed to serve you better.

faqs.question: How do businesses get started?
faqs.answer: Contact us. Integration is fast, with setup fees starting at $1,500 for community subdomains and $5,000–$10,000 for full bank, fintech, or real estate integrations.

faqs.question: Who owns customer funds on the platform?
